items.title: Genie interface and file upload enhancements

items.headline: Token-based rate limits for AI Gateway
items.summary: You can now set rate limits on model serving endpoints based on token usage.
items.why: Controls generative AI costs and fair usage across teams and applications.
items.title: Token-based rate limits now available on AI Gateway

items.headline: Serverless GPU compute adds multinode workload support
items.summary: Serverless GPU compute can now run multinode workloads across several machines, through AI Runtime.
items.why: Lets teams scale large AI training jobs across multiple GPU nodes without managing infrastructure.
items.title: Serverless GPU compute now supports multinode workloads

items.headline: OpenAI GPT OSS models now on provisioned throughput
items.summary: Databricks-hosted GPT OSS 120B and 20B models can now run on on-demand provisioned throughput Foundation Model APIs.
items.why: Offers guaranteed throughput capacity for OpenAI open-weight models on Databricks.
items.title: OpenAI GPT OSS models now supported on provisioned throughput

items.headline: Schedule jobs for Serverless GPU compute
items.summary: Users can now create and schedule jobs for Serverless GPU compute workloads.
items.why: Lets teams automate GPU training and inference runs without manual starts.
items.title: Schedule jobs for Serverless GPU compute workloads

items.headline: GPT OSS 120B and 20B models gain function calling
items.summary: Databricks-hosted GPT OSS 120B and 20B models can now call functions and tools.
items.why: Lets agents trigger external tools and APIs directly from open models on Databricks.
items.title: OpenAI GPT OSS models now support function calling

items.headline: Single-node compute now shares safely across users
items.summary: Single-node compute on standard access mode lets multiple users share one resource with full isolation.
items.why: Lets small teams share lightweight compute securely without losing user isolation.
items.title: Single-node compute on standard access mode is now GA

items.headline: Column masks now kept when replacing tables
items.summary: Replacing a table now keeps existing column masks for matching column names, even when no new mask is specified.
items.why: Stops accidental loss of column-level security during table replacement.
items.title: Column masks now retained when replacing a table

items.headline: Databricks Assistant gains user and workspace instructions
items.summary: Users can add custom instructions to tailor Assistant responses; admins can set workspace-wide instructions that take priority.
items.why: Gives teams consistent, tailored Assistant output, with admins setting standards across the workspace.
items.title: Databricks Assistant: User and workspace instructions now available

items.headline: Serverless workspaces pre-configured with compute and storage
items.summary: Serverless workspaces come pre-configured with serverless compute and default storage; account admins can enable them in the console.
items.why: Offers a fully serverless setup with no infrastructure to configure.
items.title: Serverless workspaces are now Public Preview

items.headline: Self-service access requests in Unity Catalog
items.summary: Users can now request access to discoverable Unity Catalog objects, routed to email, Slack, Teams or internal systems.
items.why: Cuts manual access tickets and lets owners approve requests where they already work.
items.title: Access requests in Unity Catalog (Public Preview)

items.headline: Jobs in continuous mode can retry failed tasks
items.summary: Jobs running in continuous mode can now retry individual tasks when they fail.
items.why: Fewer full job restarts when one task fails, keeping pipelines running.
items.title: Jobs in continuous mode can now have task-level retries for failed tasks

items.headline: Lakebase database instances now enabled by default
items.summary: The Lakebase managed Postgres preview is now on by default, so users can create instances without admin enablement.
items.why: Teams can start building Postgres databases without waiting for admin approval.
items.title: Lakebase Public Preview enabled by default

items.headline: Disable legacy features for new workspaces
items.summary: Account admins can now stop new workspaces getting DBFS root, mounts, Hive metastore, no-isolation compute and old runtimes.
items.why: Reduces risk from outdated, less secure features in new workspaces by default.
items.title: Disable legacy features for new workspaces (Public Preview)

items.headline: Unity Catalog path credential vending for external locations
items.summary: Grants short-lived credentials for external locations in your Unity Catalog metastore.
items.why: Lets teams access external storage securely without long-lived keys.
items.title: Path credential vending (Public Preview)

items.headline: Fully managed ServiceNow connector in Lakeflow Connect
items.summary: Databricks' fully managed ServiceNow ingestion connector in Lakeflow Connect is now generally available.
items.why: Lets teams ingest ServiceNow data into Databricks without building and maintaining custom pipelines.
items.title: ServiceNow connector GA

items.headline: Unity Catalog external Delta tables from third-party clients
items.summary: Customers can now create Unity Catalog external Delta tables directly from external clients such as Apache Spark.
items.why: Lets teams write governed Delta tables from Spark without leaving their existing tools.
items.title: Create external Delta tables from third-party clients (Public Preview)

items.headline: GPT OSS models gain batch inference and structured outputs
items.summary: Databricks-hosted GPT OSS 120B and 20B models now work with AI Functions for batch inference and structured outputs.
items.why: Lets teams run large-scale AI Functions with these models and enforce output formats.
items.title: Use OpenAI GPT OSS models for batch inference and structured outputs

items.headline: GPT OSS models on Mosaic AI Model Serving
items.summary: Databricks now hosts OpenAI's GPT OSS 120B and 20B models, accessible pay-per-token through Foundation Model APIs.
items.why: Gives customers open-weight OpenAI models without managing infrastructure, billed per token.
items.title: OpenAI GPT OSS models now available on Mosaic AI Model Serving

items.headline: Power BI connector adds M2M OAuth authentication
items.summary: Power BI Desktop can now authenticate with Machine-to-Machine OAuth credentials, with a new Client credentials option for service principals.
items.why: Replaces personal access tokens for service principals, improving security and reducing token management.
items.title: Power BI Databricks connector supports M2M OAuth

items.headline: Databricks ODBC driver 2.9.2 brings fixes and new features
items.summary: Version 2.9.2 adds Windows Server 2025 support, US and military domains, VOID column listing and a memory leak fix, and drops Runtime 10.4 LTS.
items.why: Keeps Excel and BI connections current; check Ubuntu 20.04 and Runtime 10.4 removals.
items.title: Databricks ODBC driver 2.9.2

items.headline: Serverless compute connects to VPC resources through PrivateLink
items.summary: Serverless compute can now connect to resources in your VPC through a network load balancer using AWS PrivateLink.
items.why: Lets serverless workloads reach internal AWS services privately, without public internet exposure.
items.title: PrivateLink connections from serverless compute to resources in your VPC through an NLB is generally available

items.headline: Genie adds local join relationships and bulk column actions
items.summary: Genie Agents can now define join relationships locally, plus bulk column show/hide and several fixes.
items.why: Authors without key permissions can still define joins for accurate answers.
items.title: Genie join relationships and data handling enhancements

items.headline: Assistant edit mode refactors code across notebook cells
items.summary: Databricks Assistant's edit mode now makes coordinated multi-step changes across several notebook cells.
items.why: Cuts repetitive prompting when refactoring larger notebooks.
items.title: Edit mode in Assistant does multi-cell code refactoring and more

items.headline: AI Playground for chatting with LLMs and prototyping apps
items.summary: AI Playground is now generally available for chatting with LLMs and prototyping AI apps.
items.why: Lets teams test models and prototype AI apps without building infrastructure.
items.title: AI Playground is now GA

items.headline: Delta Sharing supports sharing ABAC-secured tables and schemas
items.summary: Providers can now share tables and schemas protected by ABAC policies, though recipients get full access to the data.
items.why: Recipients get full access, so they must apply their own ABAC policies.
items.title: Delta Sharing supports sharing tables and schemas secured by ABAC policies (Beta)

items.headline: Easier compute policy configuration through a new UI form
items.summary: A new UI form helps configure compute policies with dropdowns, moving some settings into Advanced options and a separate tagging section.
items.why: Simplifies writing policies without memorising policy syntax; permissions now set in the policy overview.
items.title: New compute policy form (Public Preview)

items.headline: Preset date ranges for SQL editor parameters
items.summary: The new SQL editor offers preset date ranges, such as This week or Last 30 days, for timestamp, date and date range parameters.
items.why: Applies common time filters quickly without typing dates manually.
items.title: Preset date ranges for parameters in the SQL editor

items.headline: Terraform provider now manages Lakebase resources
items.summary: The Databricks Terraform provider can now create Lakebase database catalogs, database instances and synced tables as code.
items.why: Lets teams provision and manage Lakebase infrastructure through infrastructure as code.
items.title: Databricks Terraform provider supports Lakebase resources

items.headline: Delta Sharing now supports streaming tables and materialized views
items.summary: Delta Sharing can now share streaming tables and materialized views, with fewer limitations for providers and recipients.
items.why: Lets teams share live streaming data with partners more easily.
items.title: Sharing streaming tables and materialized views is GA

items.headline: Disable DBFS root and mounts in existing workspaces
items.summary: You can now disable access to the DBFS root and mounts in existing workspaces.
items.why: Reduces reliance on legacy storage and tightens data access controls.
items.title: Disable DBFS root and mounts is in Public Preview

items.headline: Notebook editing gets split view and find-and-replace
items.summary: Notebooks gain side-by-side split view, native find-and-replace across the whole notebook, and quicker switching between tab groups.
items.why: Faster editing and searching in large notebooks, with less context switching.
items.title: Improvements to the notebook editing experience

items.headline: Dashboard updates add metric view filtering and more
items.summary: Dashboard authors can now filter the Add data dialog to show only metric views, alongside undo/redo and AGGREGATE OVER custom calculations.
items.why: Makes it quicker to find metric views when building dashboards.
items.title: Dashboard performance optimizations and feature enhancements

items.headline: Move tables between Spark Declarative Pipelines
items.summary: Tables created by Spark Declarative Pipelines in Unity Catalog can now be moved from one pipeline to another.
items.why: Gives data engineers more flexibility to reorganise pipelines as ownership and workloads change.
items.title: Moving tables between Spark Declarative Pipelines on Lakeflow pipelines is now GA

items.headline: New columns in query history system table
items.summary: The query history system table now records cache origin, query parameters, and written rows and files.
items.why: Helps track query caching, parameter use and storage writes for cost and performance analysis.
items.title: New columns available in query history system table

items.headline: Inline execution history in SQL editor
items.summary: Past query results and execution history are now shown inline in the new SQL editor, with links to query profiles.
items.why: Reopen earlier results and compare run times without rerunning queries, saving time and compute.
items.title: Inline execution history in SQL editor

items.headline: Genie improves column selection and query timeouts
items.summary: Genie now picks relevant columns more accurately, auto-cancels queries over 15 minutes, and fixes Australian cross-geo and entity matching errors.
items.why: Better column picks and a 15-minute cap prevent slow, runaway queries.
items.title: Genie column selection and query improvements

items.headline: Dynamic partition overwrite with INSERT REPLACE USING
items.summary: INSERT REPLACE USING lets SQL replace matching table rows with query results, in Public Preview on Runtime 16.3.
items.why: Simpler partial table overwrites for pipelines, though preview limits USING to all partition columns.
items.title: Dynamic partition overwrite with INSERT REPLACE USING (Public Preview)

items.headline: Selectively replace table data with INSERT REPLACE ON
items.summary: INSERT REPLACE ON lets SQL replace only the table rows matching a condition, using a query result.
items.why: Enables targeted table updates without rewriting whole tables, simplifying pipeline logic.
items.title: Selectively replace data with INSERT REPLACE ON (Public Preview)

items.headline: Supervisor Agent coordinates Genie and Knowledge Assistant agents
items.summary: Supervisor Agent lets teams build multi-agent systems combining Genie Agents and Knowledge Assistant endpoints.
items.why: Lets complex tasks use specialised agents together, with SME feedback improving quality.
items.title: Supervisor Agent is in Beta

items.headline: Real-time mode arrives in Structured Streaming
items.summary: Structured Streaming gains a real-time trigger mode offering sub-second latency for operational streaming workloads that need immediate responses.
items.why: Enables sub-second streaming for operational workloads that previously needed separate, slower pipelines.
items.title: Real-time mode in Structured Streaming (Public Preview)

items.headline: Create metric views from AI/BI dashboard datasets
items.summary: Authors can now promote a dashboard dataset to a metric view directly from the AI/BI data tab.
items.why: Turns existing dashboard datasets into reusable governed metrics without rebuilding them.
items.title: New workflow for creating metric views from dashboards

items.headline: SQL editor adds date-range and multi-select parameters
items.summary: Named parameters now support date ranges and multiple values; the run button and catalog picker moved to the header.
items.why: Easier date filtering and multi-value inputs, plus more room to write queries.
items.title: SQL editor updates

items.headline: Genie improves feedback, parameters and year-over-year answers
items.summary: Genie adds editable date and numeric parameters, clearer explanations, and more accurate evaluations and year-over-year ranges.
items.why: Smoother Genie conversations and more trustworthy answers for year-over-year analysis.
items.title: Genie user experience and evaluation improvements

items.headline: Catalog Explorer lets you query tables in plain English
items.summary: Catalog Explorer's Assistant now generates SQL from natural language questions, which you can validate before running.
items.why: Lets non-SQL users explore data, with a validation step before queries run.
items.title: Explore table data using an LLM (Beta)

items.headline: CAN VIEW permission for SQL warehouses
items.summary: Users can now view SQL warehouses, including query history and profiles, without running queries.
items.why: Lets auditors and analysts monitor warehouse usage without granting query rights.
items.title: The CAN VIEW permission on SQL warehouses is now generally available

items.headline: Serverless notebooks restore Python variables after idle timeout
items.summary: Serverless notebooks now snapshot Python variables before idle termination and restore them on reconnect.
items.why: Resume long-running notebook work without losing variables or rerunning code.
items.title: Serverless notebooks: Restore Python variables after idle termination

items.headline: Enhanced Security and Compliance add-on for all customers
items.summary: Enhanced Security and Compliance add-on is available to all customers on usage-based pricing, with no contract changes.
items.why: Pay only for workspaces with enabled security features; existing contracts unaffected.
items.title: Enhanced Security and Compliance add-on now available to all customers with usage-based pricing

items.headline: Databricks connector for Power BI adds ADBC driver option
items.summary: Power BI users can now choose the ADBC driver instead of ODBC for connecting to Databricks.
items.why: Gives Power BI customers a modern driver choice for Databricks connections.
items.title: Databricks connector for Power BI now supports the ADBC driver (Public Preview)

items.headline: Git support for alerts
items.summary: Alerts in Databricks Git folders can now be tracked and managed through changes; cloned alerts start with paused schedules.
items.why: Brings alert changes under version control; cloned alerts stay paused until resumed.
items.title: Git support for alerts

items.headline: Genie adds editable filters, descriptions and notebook query suggestions
items.summary: Genie filters now show multiple values, space descriptions can be edited in place, notebook queries are suggested, and entity matching is faster.
items.why: Smoother Genie editing and better query suggestions for everyday analysts.
items.title: Genie interface, query, and data improvements

items.headline: Databricks Apps can now use Lakebase resources
items.summary: Databricks Apps now lets you add Lakebase database instances as app resources, exposed as environment variables in app code.
items.why: Simplifies connecting apps to Lakebase databases from app code.
items.title: Databricks Apps support for Lakebase resources

items.headline: Dashboards now support fifteen pages and theme import
items.summary: Dashboards now allow fifteen pages, keep theme settings on import and export, add temporal annotation lines, and restore parameterized schedules.
items.why: Bigger dashboards and preserved themes simplify sharing and reuse across teams.
items.title: Dashboard theme settings and page enhancements

items.headline: Git folders support multiple credentials per user
items.summary: Users can now add and manage multiple Git credentials in the workspace, across one or several Git providers.
items.why: Easier switching between repositories hosted on different Git providers.
items.title: Git folders now supports multiple Git credentials per user (Public Preview)

items.headline: Unity Catalog adds external lineage for outside workloads
items.summary: Unity Catalog lets you add lineage metadata for workloads run outside Databricks, such as Salesforce ingestion and Tableau or Power BI consumption.
items.why: Gives end-to-end lineage views, including Tableau and Power BI, across the whole data estate.
items.title: Bring your own data lineage (Public Preview)

items.headline: Genie API adds conversation listing and deletion
items.summary: Genie API now lets you list and delete conversations and delete Genie Agents, and Genie applies SQL functions more selectively.
items.why: Helps teams automate Genie housekeeping and get more relevant SQL answers.
items.title: Genie API enhancements and SQL function improvements

items.headline: Databricks JDBC Driver now open source
items.summary: The Databricks JDBC Driver's source code is now public under Apache 2.0, and community contributions are welcome.
items.why: Lets teams inspect, extend and contribute to connectivity used by BI tools.
items.title: New Databricks JDBC Driver is open source

items.headline: Dashboard Git diffs, Genie queries and subscriber setup
items.summary: Git diffs now show multiline queries and text, Genie supports multistatement SQL, and schedules accept subscribers at creation.
items.why: Easier review of dashboard changes and faster scheduling for stakeholders.
items.title: Dashboard Git integration and workflow improvements

items.headline: Parse documents using ai_parse_document
items.summary: Databricks adds ai_parse_document, an AI Function that extracts structured content from unstructured documents using Foundation Model APIs.
items.why: Turns unstructured documents into structured data without custom parsing pipelines.
items.title: Parse documents using ai_parse_document (Beta)

items.headline: Use PDFs in Information Extraction and Custom LLM
items.summary: Information Extraction and Custom LLM can now convert PDFs to Markdown in a table, then use that table as input.
items.why: Lets teams run extraction and custom LLM prompts on PDF documents without manual conversion.
items.title: Use PDFs in Information Extraction and Custom LLM (Beta)

items.headline: MLflow now supports compliance security profile standards
items.summary: MLflow now supports all compliance standards available on Databricks, including HIPAA, PCI-DSS and FedRAMP Moderate.
items.why: Lets regulated teams run MLflow workloads under HIPAA, PCI-DSS or FedRAMP requirements.
items.title: MLfLow support for compliance security profile standards

items.headline: File arrival triggers with file events for job runs
items.summary: Job runs can now be triggered by file events on external locations like S3, Azure and Google Cloud storage.
items.why: Raises trigger limits to 1,000 per workspace and removes the 10,000 files cap.
items.title: File arrival triggers with file events is now generally available

items.headline: OIDC federation for Delta Sharing recipients
items.summary: Open ID Connect federation for Delta Sharing lets recipients use their own identity provider's JWT tokens for short-lived, secure authentication.
items.why: Lets recipients authenticate with their own identity provider, reducing credential management for shared data.
items.title: OIDC federation for Databricks-to-open Delta Sharing is generally available

items.headline: Delta Sharing now supports managed Iceberg tables
items.summary: Delta Sharing can now share managed Iceberg tables in Databricks-to-Databricks and open sharing.
items.why: Lets teams share Iceberg tables with partners without copying data.
items.title: Sharing managed Iceberg tables in Delta Sharing is in Public Preview

items.headline: Custom rate limits for model serving endpoints
items.summary: Model serving endpoints can now have custom rate limits set for the endpoint, users, service principals or groups via AI Gateway.
items.why: Controls usage and costs by setting limits per endpoint, user, service principal or group.
items.title: Custom rate limits for model serving endpoints

items.headline: Model Serving and Mosaic AI Gateway now FIPS-compliant
items.summary: Model Serving, Foundation Model API provisioned throughput and Mosaic AI Gateway now run in FIPS-compliant environments, supporting FedRAMP Moderate and IRAP Protected B.
items.why: Lets regulated customers use AI serving under FedRAMP and Canadian compliance standards.
items.title: Expanded feature support for FIPS-Compliant environments

items.headline: Dashboards gain file upload and custom themes
items.summary: Authors can now upload files to Unity Catalog from the dashboard data tab, and customise theme fonts, backgrounds and widget colours.
items.why: Lets teams load reference data into Unity Catalog and brand dashboards consistently.
items.title: File upload and theme customization features

items.headline: Genie adds editable filters and audit log enhancements
items.summary: Genie users can edit filter values to refine answers, audit logs now record comment types, and a List Spaces API is added.
items.why: Lets teams correct Genie's filters directly and gives admins richer feedback audit trails.
items.title: Genie filter editing and audit log enhancements

items.headline: Move streaming tables and materialised views between pipelines
items.summary: Tables created by Spark Declarative Pipelines can now be moved from one pipeline to another.
items.why: Helps teams restructure pipelines without recreating their streaming tables and views.
items.title: Moving streaming tables and materialized views between pipelines is in Public Preview

items.headline: Databricks and Synapxe partner to advance Singapore healthcare data
items.summary: Synapxe, Singapore's national health tech agency, has selected Databricks to power HEALIX, supporting real-time insights, security and data democratisation.
items.why: Shows large-scale public healthcare adoption of Databricks for AI and data democratisation.
items.title: Databricks and Synapxe Join Forces to Accelerate Data and AI-Enabled Innovation in Singapore’s Public Healthcare Sector

items.headline: Databricks and Google Cloud partner to bring Gemini natively
items.summary: Databricks and Google Cloud have agreed a strategic partnership to make Gemini models available natively within the Databricks platform.
items.why: Gives customers Gemini models directly inside their data and AI workflows, without moving data.
items.title: Databricks Announces Strategic AI Partnership with Google Cloud to Bring Gemini Models Natively to the Data + AI Platform

items.headline: Databricks and Microsoft extend partnership for Azure Databricks
items.summary: Databricks and Microsoft have agreed a multi-year deal to advance data and AI innovation on Azure Databricks.
items.why: Signals deeper Azure investment and roadmap commitment for Databricks customers on Microsoft cloud.
items.title: Databricks and Microsoft Extend Strategic Partnership for Azure Databricks

items.headline: Attribute-based access control in Unity Catalog
items.summary: Unity Catalog now offers tag-driven access policies across catalogs, schemas and tables, applied via tags and user-defined functions.
items.why: Lets governance teams set policies once across large data estates, reducing manual access work.
items.title: Attribute-based access control (ABAC) in Unity Catalog is in Beta

items.headline: Automatic liquid clustering for Unity Catalog managed tables
items.summary: Unity Catalog managed tables can now use automatic liquid clustering, which picks clustering keys to optimise data layout.
items.why: Less manual tuning of table layout to keep query performance strong.
items.title: Automatic liquid clustering is now GA

items.headline: Unity Catalog adds open table interoperability and business semantics
items.summary: Unity Catalog now supports Apache Iceberg and Delta Lake across compute engines, adding unified semantics and discovery for business users.
items.why: Avoids table format lock-in and gives business users governed, self-service semantics and discovery.
items.title: Databricks Eliminates Table Format Lock-in and Adds Capabilities for Business Users with Unity Catalog Advancements

items.headline: Databricks donates Declarative Pipelines to Apache Spark
items.summary: Databricks is open-sourcing its core declarative ETL framework as Apache Spark Declarative Pipelines.
items.why: Lets teams use the same pipeline framework in open-source Spark.
items.title: Databricks Donates Declarative Pipelines to Apache Spark™ Open Source Project

items.headline: Lakeflow Designer brings no-code pipeline building to analysts
items.summary: Databricks announced an upcoming preview of Lakeflow Designer, a no-code ETL tool with drag-and-drop building and a GenAI assistant.
items.why: Lets non-technical staff build production pipelines without coding.
items.title: Databricks Unveils Lakeflow Designer for Data Analysts to Build Reliable Pipelines Without Coding

items.headline: Databricks Free Edition and $100 million talent investment
items.summary: Databricks has released a free edition of its Data + AI Platform and committed $100 million to developing data and AI talent.
items.why: Gives customers a low-cost route to build data and AI skills.
items.title: Databricks Launches Free Edition and Announces $100 Million Investment to Develop the Next Generation of Data and AI Talent

items.headline: Databricks One brings data and AI to business users
items.summary: Databricks has launched Databricks One, a new experience giving every business user access to data and AI.
items.why: Lets business teams use data and AI without relying on technical specialists.
items.title: Databricks Unveils Databricks One: A New Experience to Bring Data and AI to Every Corner of the Business

items.headline: Agent Bricks: a new way to build AI agents
items.summary: Databricks introduces Agent Bricks, which automatically optimises AI agents using customers' own data for cost-efficient, trustworthy results.
items.why: Lets teams build cheaper, more reliable AI agents on their own data.
items.title: Databricks Launches Agent Bricks: A New Approach to Building AI Agents

items.headline: Databricks unveils Lakebase, a managed Postgres database for AI
items.summary: Databricks has announced Lakebase, a fully managed Postgres database built for AI apps and agents, adding an operational layer to its platform.
items.why: Gives customers an operational database alongside their data and AI platform for building agents.
items.title: Databricks Launches Lakebase: a New Class of Operational Database for AI Apps and Agents

items.headline: AI Gateway for governing and monitoring AI models
items.summary: Mosaic AI Gateway reaches general availability, adding governance, monitoring, rate limiting, and traffic routing for model serving endpoints.
items.why: Centralises governance, monitoring and cost tracking for AI models in production.
items.title: AI Gateway is now generally available

items.headline: Read foreign Apache Iceberg tables via Lakehouse Federation
items.summary: You can now read Iceberg tables from foreign catalogues such as HMS, Glue and Snowflake Horizon, with Unity Catalog governance.
items.why: Query Iceberg data across catalogues without copying it, keeping fine-grained access controls.
items.title: Foreign Apache Iceberg tables are in Public Preview

items.headline: Faster Databricks SQL Serverless engine rolling out globally
items.summary: Serverless SQL warehouses get automatic engine upgrades, delivering up to 25% faster dashboards, ETL and mixed workloads.
items.why: Faster queries at no extra cost, with no configuration needed.
items.title: Databricks SQL Serverless engine upgrades

items.headline: Admins can now monitor and revoke personal access tokens
items.summary: Account admins can now review and revoke personal access tokens from the account console's token report page.
items.why: Helps admins tighten security, though Databricks recommends moving to OAuth tokens instead.
items.title: Monitor and revoke personal access tokens in your account (GA)

items.headline: AUTO CDC APIs replace APPLY CHANGES in pipelines
items.summary: New AUTO CDC APIs handle change data feeds in Spark Declarative Pipelines, and Databricks recommends moving away from APPLY CHANGES.
items.why: Databricks advises migrating, so existing CDC pipelines should be updated.
items.title: AUTO CDC APIs replace APPLY CHANGES

items.headline: Convert Unity Catalog external tables to managed tables
items.summary: ALTER TABLE ... SET MANAGED lets customers convert Unity Catalog external tables to managed tables, now in Public Preview.
items.why: Unlocks managed table governance, reliability and performance for participating customers.
items.title: Convert to Unity Catalog managed table from external table is in Public Preview

items.headline: Microsoft SharePoint connector in Lakeflow Connect
items.summary: Lakeflow Connect now offers a fully managed SharePoint connector for ingesting data, with API-based pipeline creation only.
items.why: Brings SharePoint content into Databricks without building custom ingestion pipelines.
items.title: Microsoft SharePoint connector (Beta)

items.headline: Model Context Protocol support for AI agents
items.summary: Databricks now supports MCP, an open standard letting AI agents securely access tools and data through Unity Catalog, via managed or custom servers.
items.why: Lets agents reach Unity Catalog data securely without custom integration work.
items.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP) for AI agents is in Beta

items.headline: MLflow 3.0 brings tracking and observability for AI agents
items.summary: MLflow 3.0 is now generally available, offering experiment tracking, observability and evaluation for models, AI applications and agents.
items.why: Gives teams one place to track, monitor and evaluate ML and agent work.
items.title: MLflow 3.0 is generally available

items.headline: Deployment jobs automate model evaluation and deployment
items.summary: Deployment jobs automate evaluation, approval and deployment whenever a new model version is created.
items.why: Cuts manual steps in releasing models, integrating with Unity Catalog and Lakeflow Jobs.
items.title: Deployment jobs (Public Preview)

items.headline: Serverless performance setting for jobs and pipelines
items.summary: Jobs and pipelines can now choose performance-optimised or cost-optimised serverless modes, for faster startup or lower cost.
items.why: Lets you trade startup speed against cost on serverless workloads.
items.title: Serverless performance targets is now GA

items.headline: Manage network policies for serverless egress control
items.summary: Admins can set and enforce outbound network policies for serverless compute, with dry-run mode and denial logs in Unity Catalog.
items.why: Controls where serverless workloads can send data, reducing exfiltration risk and aiding audits.
items.title: Manage network policies for serverless egress control (Generally Available)

items.headline: Cross-platform view sharing via Delta Sharing
items.summary: Delta Sharing now shares views across platforms, with updated billing, a materialisation history table and configurable TTL.
items.why: Enables sharing views with other platforms and tracking materialised data costs.
items.title: Cross-platform view sharing is now GA

items.headline: Configure PrivateLink from serverless compute to S3 buckets
items.summary: Serverless compute can now reach S3 buckets over AWS PrivateLink, keeping traffic off the public internet.
items.why: Keeps serverless data access on private networks, improving security posture.
items.title: Configure PrivateLink connections from serverless compute to S3 Storage buckets (Public Preview)

items.headline: Tag policies enforce consistent tagging across data assets
items.summary: Admins can now enforce consistent tags on catalogs, schemas and tables, controlling which users can assign them.
items.why: Standardises metadata for classification, cost tracking and access control.
items.title: Tag policies is in Beta

items.headline: Serverless GPU compute for deep learning training
items.summary: Serverless GPU compute now supports custom single and multi-node deep learning workloads, including training and fine-tuning models.
items.why: Train and fine-tune custom deep learning models without managing GPU infrastructure.
items.title: Serverless GPU compute is in Beta

items.headline: Databricks Apps supports compliance security profile standards
items.summary: Databricks Apps now meets all compliance security profile standards, including HIPAA, PCI-DSS and FedRAMP Moderate.
items.why: Lets regulated customers run Apps workloads under HIPAA, PCI-DSS and FedRAMP requirements.
items.title: Databricks Apps support for compliance security profile standards

items.headline: PrivateLink from serverless compute to VPC resources
items.summary: Serverless compute can now reach resources in your VPC through a network load balancer using AWS PrivateLink.
items.why: Keeps serverless workloads reaching private AWS resources without traffic crossing the public internet.
items.title: PrivateLink connections from serverless compute to resources in your VPC through an NLB is in Public Preview

items.headline: Admins can grant consumer access entitlement
items.summary: Workspace admins can now grant consumer access to users, service principals and groups, enabling limited UI access, BI tool queries and dashboard viewing.
items.why: Lets BI users query warehouses and view dashboards through a dedicated entitlement.
items.title: Consumer access entitlement is generally available

items.headline: Genie adds entity matching and fixes SQL editor
items.summary: Genie now supports up to 60 entity matching columns, and a chat SQL editor bug is fixed.
items.why: Lets teams match more business terms accurately, and the SQL editor works reliably again.
items.title: Genie entity matching and SQL editor improvements

items.headline: Salesforce Data Cloud file sharing connector
items.summary: Adds a zero-copy file federation option for querying Salesforce Data Cloud, reading files directly without JDBC.
items.why: Better performance for large Salesforce datasets than query federation, with stronger pushdown.
items.title: Salesforce Data Cloud File Sharing connector (Public Preview)

items.headline: History sharing now on by default for Delta Sharing
items.summary: History sharing is now enabled by default in Databricks Runtime 16.2 and above, speeding up Databricks-to-Databricks Delta Sharing table reads.
items.why: Faster reads on shared tables, applied automatically on Runtime 16.2 and above.
items.title: History sharing now enabled by default to improve table read performance for Databricks-to-Databricks Delta Sharing (GA)

items.headline: Storage-optimised endpoints for Mosaic AI Vector Search
items.summary: Vector Search adds storage-optimised endpoints with billion-vector capacity and 10-20x faster indexing.
items.why: Supports far larger vector collections with faster indexing and optimised pricing for scale.
items.title: Mosaic AI Vector Search storage-optimized endpoints are Public Preview

items.headline: Unity Catalog HTTP connections support per-user OAuth
items.summary: Users can now sign into external services with their own OAuth credentials through HTTP connections, instead of one shared credential.
items.why: Lets each user authenticate separately, improving accountability for external service access.
items.title: Unity Catalog HTTP connections support OAuth User-to-Machine Per User credentials (Public Preview)

items.headline: Unity Catalog metric views for consistent business metrics
items.summary: Unity Catalog metric views let teams define core business metrics once and reuse them across dashboards, Genie Agents and alerts.
items.why: Gives one governed definition of KPIs, so reports across tools agree.
items.title: Metric views are in Public Preview

items.headline: Genie knowledge store adds richer table metadata controls
items.summary: Authors can now edit descriptions, add column synonyms, hide columns and get format assistance in Genie spaces.
items.why: Makes Genie answers more accurate by giving it clearer data context.
items.title: Genie knowledge store and metadata improvements

items.headline: Databricks SQL editor gains snippets, drafts and filters
items.summary: New queries open in Drafts, reusable query snippets are added, audit events are logged, and filters now update visualisations.
items.why: Speeds up SQL authoring and lets analysts explore results interactively without rewriting queries.
items.title: User interface updates

items.headline: Catalog and schema picker for dashboard datasets
items.summary: Draft dashboards can now select a catalog and schema in the dataset editor, so queries can use table names alone. A full-screen widget global filter fix is also included.
items.why: Shorter table references make dashboard queries quicker to write and easier to maintain.
items.title: Dashboard catalog picker and filter fixes

items.headline: New version of Databricks SQL alerts
items.summary: A new alerts version combines query setup, conditions, schedules and notifications in one interface; legacy alerts remain available.
items.why: Simpler alert creation and management, with legacy alerts still supported.
items.title: New alert version in Beta

items.headline: Dashboard filter and visualisation improvements
items.summary: Dashboards gain a global filters panel, include or exclude filter values, constant reference lines, and cleaner PDF snapshots.
items.why: Makes dashboards easier to filter and present to executives.
items.title: Dashboard filter enhancements and visualization improvements

items.headline: Genie adds usage guidance and faster query results
items.summary: Genie now supports usage guidance for SQL examples, shows results sooner, and fixes empty visualisations.
items.why: Faster answers and clearer example SQL make Genie more useful for everyday questions.
items.title: Genie usage guidance and query performance

items.headline: AI/BI dashboards get query, schedule and formatting updates
items.summary: Genie now queries only dashboard datasets, adds null-check calculations, supports schedules without embedded credentials, and carries over number formatting.
items.why: Keeps dashboards accurate, scheduled and consistently formatted with fewer manual fixes.
items.title: Dashboard query updates and calculation support

items.headline: Databricks agrees to acquire Neon
items.summary: Databricks announced its intent to acquire Neon, a serverless Postgres company, to expand its database offering for developers and AI agents.
items.why: Signals Lakebase's serverless Postgres foundation and a major acquisition shaping Databricks' database strategy.
items.title: Databricks Agrees to Acquire Neon to Deliver Serverless Postgres for Developers + AI Agents

items.headline: Genie adds larger entity matching and point maps
items.summary: Genie entity matching now handles 1024 values per column, up from 255, and Genie supports point maps.
items.why: Lets Genie answer questions over high-cardinality fields and map data more accurately.
items.title: Genie entity matching and point map support

items.headline: Dashboards gain AI-assisted point maps and multi-table selection
items.summary: Dashboards now generate point maps from natural-language prompts, add multiple tables at once, and support dashboard tasks in bundles.
items.why: Lets teams build map visuals faster and deploy dashboards through automated jobs.
items.title: Dashboard data selection and point maps

items.headline: Databricks launches data intelligence for marketing
items.summary: Databricks launches a unified data and AI foundation bringing customer and campaign data together for marketers.
items.why: Lets marketers self-serve audience insights and run more relevant, efficient campaigns.
items.title: Databricks Unveils Data Intelligence for Marketing

items.headline: Genie suggests follow-up questions for text responses
items.summary: Genie now suggests follow-up questions for text-only responses, and its instruction following has been refined.
items.why: Helps users keep exploring data, and Genie follows relevant instructions more reliably.
items.title: Genie follow-up questions and instruction processing

items.headline: Genie gets sharper prompts and clearer permission messages
items.summary: Genie uses a shorter top-k prompt, clearer permission warnings and collapsible charts, and admins can enable prompt matching from Previews.
items.why: Better answers and clearer guidance when access is missing.
items.title: Genie prompt improvements and prompt matching

items.headline: Dashboard choropleth maps and AI forecast for line charts
items.summary: Dashboards now support choropleth maps coloured by metrics such as population or income, and line charts can generate AI forecasts in public preview.
items.why: Lets teams map regional performance and add forecasts to trend charts without extra tools.
items.title: Dashboard choropleth maps and AI forecast

items.headline: MUFG Bank selects Databricks as next-generation AI platform
items.summary: MUFG Bank has chosen Databricks as its next-generation data and AI platform, consolidating scattered AI model development.
items.why: Shows a major global bank consolidating its AI development onto one shared platform.
items.title: MUFG Bank Adopts Databricks as Its Next-Generation Data and AI Platform

items.headline: Databricks invests over US$250 million in India
items.summary: Databricks commits over US$250 million to India over three years, launching a data and AI academy and a Bengaluru R&D office.
items.why: Signals local investment in skills, talent and R&D for India-based customers.
items.title: Databricks to Invest Over US$250 Million in India over the Next Three Years to Advance Data and AI Innovation in the Country

items.headline: Custom dimensions and pivot table improvements for AI/BI dashboards
items.summary: Authors can now add custom dimensions using CASE WHEN, CONCAT and COALESCE, plus resizable pivot tables and smoother Sankey charts.
items.why: Lets teams build calculated fields directly in dashboards without changing source data.
items.title: Dashboard custom dimensions and pivot table improvements

items.headline: Genie adds example questions and table clean-up
items.summary: Genie now suggests example and follow-up questions, lets users remove inaccessible tables, and restricts table picks to tables with SELECT access.
items.why: Helps Genie Agents return results and keeps table access transparent.
items.title: Genie example questions and table management

items.headline: Genie gets feedback revamp and customer-managed keys
items.summary: Genie feedback now lets users explain errors and regenerate or send responses for review, and supports customer-managed keys.
items.why: Stronger encryption control for Genie data, and better answer correction for teams.
items.title: Genie feedback workflow and security enhancements

items.headline: Git version control for dashboards
items.summary: Dashboards can now be linked to Git folders for version control, and draft dashboards can be reverted to their last published state.
items.why: Track dashboard changes and undo edits, making collaboration safer across teams.
items.title: Dashboard source control and export fixes

items.headline: Legacy dashboards can no longer be created or cloned
items.summary: Legacy dashboards can no longer be created or cloned via the UI or API; Databricks recommends AI/BI dashboards.
items.why: Migrate existing work to AI/BI dashboards; security fixes and outage support continue.
items.title: End of support for legacy dashboards

items.headline: AI/BI dashboard publishing and visualisation updates
items.summary: Publishing now embeds the publisher's warehouse permission, and Genie chats resume, plus Sankey charts and map PNG downloads.
items.why: Simplifies sharing dashboards without forcing individual warehouse access for every viewer.
items.title: Dashboard publishing and visualization updates

items.headline: CAN VIEW permission for SQL warehouses
items.summary: Lets users monitor SQL warehouses, including query history and profiles, without being able to run queries.
items.why: Gives admins finer control over who can monitor warehouses without running queries.
items.title: CAN VIEW permission for SQL warehouses is in Public Preview

items.headline: Custom autoformatting options for SQL queries
items.summary: You can now customise how SQL queries are autoformatted across all queries.
items.why: Keeps SQL formatting consistent across teams without manual tidying.
items.title: Custom autoformatting options for SQL queries

items.headline: AI/BI dashboards get migration and localisation improvements
items.summary: Adds locale-specific settings, fixes dual-axis migration, improves URL stability, and simplifies Genie Agent setup.
items.why: Smoother migrations and fewer broken links for dashboards serving multiple locales.
items.title: Dashboard migration and localization improvements

items.headline: Databricks and Anthropic partner to bring Claude models
items.summary: Databricks and Anthropic have signed a multi-year partnership to bring Claude models to the Databricks platform.
items.why: Lets over 10,000 customers build secure AI agents with Claude on their enterprise data.
items.title: Databricks and Anthropic Sign Landmark Deal to Bring Claude Models to the Data + AI Platform

items.headline: Genie Agent gets redesigned UI and permission controls
items.summary: Genie Agent has a redesigned authoring and chat interface, and authors can only add tables they can access.
items.why: Clearer permissions and better SQL matching improve answer quality and governance for analysts.
items.title: Genie Agent (formerly Genie Space) redesign and permission management

items.headline: Genie Conversation API for programmatic data questions
items.summary: Developers can now ask questions, retrieve generated SQL and results, and query Genie Agents via API.
items.why: Lets teams embed Genie's natural language answers into their own apps.
items.title: Genie conversation API and prompt matching

items.headline: Dashboards gain audit logs and workflow task support
items.summary: Dashboard PDF downloads now write an audit log event, dashboards can run as workflow tasks, and filters support sorting.
items.why: Improves governance tracking and automates dashboard refreshes and subscription emails.
items.title: Dashboard audit logs and workflow integration

items.headline: Palantir and Databricks announce strategic AI product partnership
items.summary: Palantir and Databricks are combining Palantir's AIP with the Databricks Data + AI Platform to speed up production AI applications and cut costs.
items.why: A major partner alliance may simplify building and running secure AI applications on Databricks.
items.title: Palantir and Databricks Announce Strategic Product Partnership to Deliver Secure and Efficient AI to Customers

items.headline: Genie benchmarks now detect incorrect results more accurately
items.summary: Genie's benchmark evaluation now more accurately flags incorrect answers.
items.why: Helps teams trust Genie's accuracy checks before rolling out to users.
items.title: Genie benchmark evaluation improvements

items.headline: Dashboard date controls and Genie chart questions
items.summary: Dashboards gain current-day relative dates, publish notifications, and Genie questions about specific charts.
items.why: Lets users ask Genie about individual charts and keeps stakeholders informed of dashboard updates.
items.title: Dashboard date controls and notification features

items.headline: Genie adds CSV and Excel file uploads
items.summary: Users can upload CSV and Excel files directly to a Genie Agent, available on request via account teams.
items.why: Brings ad hoc spreadsheet data into Genie for quick questions alongside governed data.
items.title: Genie file uploads and formatting improvements

items.headline: Databricks achieves FedRAMP High authorisation on AWS GovCloud
items.summary: Databricks has received FedRAMP High authorisation for its platform on AWS GovCloud, meeting strict US government security requirements.
items.why: Lets US federal and public sector customers run sensitive workloads on Databricks.
items.title: Databricks Achieves FedRAMP High Authorization for AWS GovCloud

items.headline: Genie adds parameter editing and data source visibility
items.summary: Users can now edit parameters behind a trusted-question response, see source tables for each answer, and cancel queries while waiting for a warehouse.
items.why: Helps analysts trust answers and avoid wasted waiting time on slow queries.
items.title: Genie parameter editing and data source visibility

items.headline: Dashboard thumbnails and larger pivot tables
items.summary: Dashboards now show thumbnails for popular ones, pivot tables handle 1,000 rows and columns, and box plots allow Y-axis renaming.
items.why: Faster navigation and bigger pivot tables help teams explore larger datasets.
items.title: Dashboard thumbnails and table enhancements

items.headline: Catalog Explorer adds asset metadata and query-only filtering
items.summary: Hovering over an asset in the schema browser now shows its Unity Catalog metadata, and a Can query filter hides view-only objects.
items.why: Helps users find data they can actually query, and see context faster.
items.title: User interface updates

items.headline: Databricks introduces SAP Databricks inside SAP Business Data Cloud
items.summary: Databricks has released SAP Databricks, a product natively integrated into SAP Business Data Cloud.
items.why: Gives SAP customers native Databricks capability within their existing SAP data estate.
items.title: Databricks Announces Launch of SAP Databricks

items.headline: Databricks acquires BladeBridge to speed up warehouse migrations
items.summary: Databricks acquires BladeBridge's technology and team to support migrations to Databricks SQL.
items.why: Eases moving legacy warehouses to Databricks SQL, now at a $600 million run rate.
items.title: Databricks Acquires BladeBridge Technology and Talent to Accelerate Data Warehouse Migrations

items.headline: Databricks secures $15B financing to attract AI talent
items.summary: Databricks completed a $10B Series J equity round and closed $5.25B in additional debt financing.
items.why: Signals substantial investment to fund AI talent and global expansion.
items.title: Databricks Announces $15B in Financing to Attract Top AI Talent and Accelerate Global Expansion

items.headline: Improved charts arrive in notebooks and SQL editor
items.summary: The new chart system brings faster performance, better colour schemes and quicker interactivity in notebooks and SQL editor.
items.why: Faster, clearer charts for everyday analysis in notebooks and SQL editor.
items.title: Chart visualization updates

items.headline: New SQL editor adds download, shortcut and tab improvements
items.summary: The new SQL editor gains automatic download naming, font-size shortcuts, @mentions in comments, faster tabs and clearer warehouse sizes.
items.why: Smoother daily querying, quicker collaboration and easier warehouse selection for analysts.
items.title: SQL editor user interface updates

digests.title: Genie gains editable filters and richer audit logs
digests.intro: Databricks has made Genie more practical for analysts by letting users edit filter values to refine answers without starting again. For data leaders, the update also brings better governance, as audit logs now record Genie comment types. Together, these changes make conversational analytics easier to tune and easier to oversee.

digests.title: Genie Agent gets a redesign and tighter permissions
digests.intro: Databricks has redesigned the Genie Agent interface, making it easier to work with. Editors can now view the source SQL behind answers, improving transparency for data teams. Authors are also limited to adding tables they already have access to, strengthening governance over what Genie can query.

digests.title: Genie gains smarter questions and tighter table controls
digests.intro: Databricks has upgraded Genie, its natural language analytics assistant, so it now suggests example questions drawn from table metadata. Users can also tidy their workspace by removing tables they can no longer access. The table picker now enforces SELECT privileges, helping data leaders keep access governed without slowing self-service analysis.

digests.title: Genie gains parameter editing and clearer source visibility
digests.intro: Databricks has extended Genie, its conversational analytics tool, with the ability to edit response parameters and view the source tables behind each answer. Users can also cancel queries while waiting for a warehouse, giving data leaders greater transparency and control over how business questions are answered.

digests.title: Genie now suggests follow-up questions and follows instructions better
digests.intro: Databricks has extended Genie, its conversational analytics assistant, so it now proposes follow-up questions even when a text answer carries no SQL or results. Genie also follows user instructions more reliably, which should make natural language exploration of data more dependable for analysts and business users alike.

digests.title: Genie gains guidance and faster query results
digests.intro: Databricks has upgraded Genie, its natural language analytics assistant, with usage guidance for SQL examples. Results now appear sooner, and a rendering fault that left some visualisations empty has been fixed. For data leaders, this means quicker, more reliable self-service analysis for business users.

digests.title: Genie gains file uploads and chart-level answers
digests.intro: Genie is becoming more useful for everyday analysis. A gated preview lets users upload CSV and Excel files straight into a Genie Agent, while published dashboards can now answer questions about a selected chart. Contact your account team to enable file uploads.

digests.title: Stronger governance meets agentic AI access
digests.intro: This period's updates focus on trust and control across the Databricks estate. Certification tags and context-based ingress rules give data leaders clearer signals on asset quality and tighter control over who can reach workspaces. Meanwhile, GPT-5 models in Public Preview and a managed SQL MCP server extend governed Unity Catalog data to AI agents.

digests.title: Governed data access and agents extend across platforms
digests.intro: This period's updates extend Databricks capabilities into the wider AI and data estate. Genie Agents can now be used as tools in Microsoft Copilot Studio, while Unity Catalog adds governed JDBC connections to external databases. Mosaic AI Model Serving also now hosts OpenAI GPT-5.1, with pay-per-token, reasoning, vision and batch AI Functions support.

digests.title: Unity Catalog opens tables to external engines
digests.intro: Compatibility Mode is the standout update this period, letting external engines read Unity Catalog tables directly. It generates read-only, automatically synced copies of tables and views for Delta and Iceberg clients such as Athena, Snowflake and Fabric. For data leaders, this widens tool choice while Unity Catalog remains the central point for governance.

digests.title: Governed sharing, agentic analytics and real-time collaboration
digests.intro: This period's updates centre on governance and collaboration. Attribute-based access control can now protect tables and schemas shared through Delta Sharing, in preview, extending policy beyond your own platform. Genie's Create and Update APIs enter Beta, and Research Agent now handles multi-step reasoning for complex business questions, while teams can co-edit notebook cells in real time.

digests.title: Governed discovery and tighter access controls
digests.intro: This period's updates focus on making governed data easier to find and safer to use. Unity Catalog's Discover page and business domains help teams search and curate trusted data, while scoped access tokens limit API permissions. Power BI's new default ADBC driver and Claude Sonnet 4.6 on Mosaic AI add performance and model choice.

digests.title: Lakebase gains autoscaling, branching and scale-to-zero
digests.intro: Lakebase now offers autoscaling compute, scale-to-zero, database branching and instant restore on AWS, free for a limited time. Databricks also hosts OpenAI's GPT-5.2 through Foundation Model APIs, while Vector Search reranking is now generally available. Auto Loader's file events add faster file discovery for data engineers.

digests.title: Natural language querying and metric views arrive in Databricks
digests.intro: Databricks is making data access more conversational, with Catalog Explorer's Assistant generating SQL from plain English questions that users can validate before running. Teams can also promote AI/BI dashboard datasets directly into metric views, giving analysts a reusable, governed layer for business metrics.

digests.title: Knowledge Assistant now generally available in US
digests.intro: Knowledge Assistant is now generally available in select US regions, letting teams build chatbots that answer questions over their documents with citations. For data leaders, this offers a practical route to giving staff trusted, traceable answers from internal content. Checking regional availability before planning rollouts will help keep deployment on track.

digests.title: Agent mode arrives in Databricks Assistant
digests.intro: Databricks Assistant's new Agent mode now carries out multi-step tasks from a single prompt, and it is enabled by default for most customers. Data leaders should review this default with their administrators, as admins can switch it off where governance or cost policies require. This moves the assistant from answering questions towards completing work.

digests.title: Claude Opus 4.5 arrives on Databricks Model Serving
digests.intro: Databricks now hosts Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.5 through Mosaic AI Model Serving, available on pay-per-token Foundation Model APIs. The model suits reasoning, vision and batch workloads, letting teams add advanced generative capability without managing their own infrastructure. For data leaders, this widens model choice inside the governed lakehouse.

digests.title: Wider agent reach with tighter governance
digests.intro: Updates this period extend Databricks beyond its own walls while tightening control. Agents can now reach external MCP servers, and dashboards can be embedded for external users in Public Preview. Governed tags and OAuth token federation give data leaders firmer control over assets and access.

digests.title: Open sharing and governance extend beyond Databricks
digests.intro: Databricks has widened its open data story, with Delta Sharing now covering managed Iceberg tables. Unity Catalog adds external lineage for workloads run outside the platform, giving teams end-to-end visibility. Meanwhile, ai_parse_document turns unstructured documents into structured content using Foundation Model APIs.

digests.title: OpenAI's open models and easier Power BI authentication
digests.intro: OpenAI's GPT OSS 120B and 20B models now sit on Mosaic AI Model Serving, available pay-per-token through Foundation Model APIs. Power BI Desktop also supports Machine-to-Machine OAuth, with a Client credentials option for service principals. Together, these widen model choice and simplify secure access for data leaders.

digests.title: Serverless and AI tooling take centre stage
digests.intro: Databricks Assistant can now run fully on Databricks-hosted models across all clouds, at no extra cost. Serverless continues to expand, with multinode GPU workloads through AI Runtime and workspaces that arrive pre-configured with compute and storage. Self-service access requests in Unity Catalog and a collaborative SQL editor also speed up everyday work.

digests.title: Multi-agent coordination and real-time streaming arrive
digests.intro: This period brings the Supervisor Agent, which lets teams coordinate Genie and Knowledge Assistant agents within a single multi-agent system. Structured Streaming also gains a real-time trigger mode with sub-second latency for operational workloads that need immediate responses. Dashboard authors benefit from metric view filtering, undo and redo, and AGGREGATE OVER custom calculations.

digests.title: Databricks Assistant gains coordinated multi-cell editing
digests.intro: Databricks Assistant's new edit mode can now make coordinated, multi-step changes across several notebook cells in one go. For data leaders, this points to faster refactoring and less manual rework when maintaining analytics code, though teams should still review AI-generated changes before they reach production.

digests.title: Metric views and Genie gain new capabilities
digests.intro: Metric views are becoming central to how Databricks delivers governed analytics. Dashboards now show metric view lineage, Genie Agents expose metric view names and a Context tab, and Serverless 18.0 adds SQL window functions to metric views. Unity Catalog's new commands also let teams set business metadata such as display names and synonyms on columns.

digests.title: Account-wide governance and richer dashboards
digests.intro: Governance takes a significant step as attribute-based access control now applies policies account-wide across attached workspaces. Analytics teams gain dashboards that read metric view formatting, plus per-widget date and number range filters. Together, these updates let data leaders enforce consistent controls while delivering more precise self-service reporting.

digests.title: Enhanced security add-on now open to all customers
digests.intro: This period's headline is the Enhanced Security and Compliance add-on, now available to every customer on usage-based pricing without any contract changes. For analysts and BI teams, the Power BI connector now offers the ADBC driver as an alternative to ODBC when connecting to Databricks. Together, these updates make stronger governance and simpler connectivity easier to adopt.

digests.title: Databricks Assistant skills and richer dashboards
digests.intro: Databricks Assistant can now create skills that extend its Agent mode with domain-specific capabilities, loaded automatically when relevant. Dashboards gain pivoted Excel downloads, pivot table total rows, resizable widgets and better multi-select paste. Together, these updates help data teams tailor AI assistance and deliver more polished reporting.

digests.title: Workspace editing, deployment and multimodal AI serving
digests.intro: This period brings practical gains across the platform. Teams can now edit and deploy Declarative Automation Bundles directly in the workspace, testing and committing changes together. Mosaic AI Model Serving also accepts multimodal inputs for hosted foundation models, covering real-time and batch inference, while the Google Sheets connector gains saved queries.

digests.title: Zero-copy data sharing with SAP Business Data Cloud
digests.intro: Databricks now connects directly with SAP Business Data Cloud, enabling secure, zero-copy data sharing in both directions. For data leaders, this removes the need to duplicate SAP data across platforms, lowering cost and latency while keeping governance intact. It is a practical step towards unifying enterprise and analytical data estates.

digests.title: Genie gains feedback tools and customer-managed keys
digests.intro: Databricks has overhauled Genie feedback, letting users explain errors and regenerate or send responses for review. Genie now also supports customer-managed keys, strengthening control over sensitive data. Together, these changes give data leaders better quality assurance and tighter security for natural-language analytics.

digests.title: Native Excel file reading arrives in Databricks
digests.intro: Databricks can now read Excel files directly into Spark DataFrames, removing the need for external libraries. For data leaders, this simplifies ingesting spreadsheet data from business teams, with fewer dependencies to maintain. Teams can bring familiar Excel sources into their pipelines with less friction.

digests.title: Secure agent connectivity and simpler serverless workspaces
digests.intro: Databricks has made it easier for AI agents to connect securely to platform resources and external APIs through managed MCP servers. Alongside this, serverless workspaces now arrive pre-configured with serverless compute and default storage, offering a fully managed SaaS experience. Together, these changes reduce integration effort and speed up the path from experimentation to production for data teams.

digests.title: Procedural SQL and multi-agent AI take centre stage
digests.intro: SQL scripting is now generally available in Databricks SQL 2025.40, bringing conditionals, loops, local variables and exception handling to the warehouse. Alongside it, Supervisor Agent lets teams build multi-agent systems that coordinate agents and tools, currently in select US regions. Together these updates let data leaders move more logic into governed SQL and automate complex AI-driven tasks.

digests.title: Natural language and agents take centre stage
digests.intro: Natural language is now central to Databricks, with Catalog Explorer generating SQL and Supervisor Agent coordinating Genie and Knowledge Assistant agents. Metric views and richer dashboard tools give analysts reusable, governed building blocks, while real-time mode brings sub-second latency to Structured Streaming. Usage-based customers can also add enhanced security and compliance without changing contracts.

digests.title: Governance extends across accounts, sharing and AI agents
digests.intro: Attribute-based access control now applies account-wide, and ABAC policies extend to Delta Sharing in preview. Frontier models from Anthropic and OpenAI are hosted on Databricks, and Genie Agents now work inside Microsoft Copilot Studio. Together, these updates let data leaders govern data and AI consistently across workspaces and partners.

digests.title: Broader access and serverless GPU training arrive
digests.intro: This period brings two notable steps towards wider use of the Databricks platform. Workspace admins can now grant consumer access to users, service principals and groups, letting more people query data through BI tools, view dashboards and use the UI in a limited way. Serverless GPU compute also supports custom single and multi-node deep learning, including training and fine-tuning models.

digests.title: Databricks deepens SAP integration and agent connectivity
digests.intro: The biggest story is the deeper SAP partnership, which eases access to SAP data across SAP Business Data Cloud and SAP Databricks. Alongside it, governance and reliability advanced, with schema-level anomaly detection, general availability for real-time pipelines and clearer metric view relationships. AI connectivity also widened through default OAuth for external agents and GPT-6.1 Terra on Unity Gateway.

digests.title: Richer context and shared metrics for Genie
digests.intro: Databricks is making its AI and analytics layers easier to govern and trust. Genie spaces now offer far richer table metadata, letting authors refine descriptions, synonyms and visibility. Unity Catalog metric views complete the picture by defining core business metrics once for dashboards, Genie Agents and alerts.

digests.title: Better monitoring and change tracking across Databricks
digests.intro: This period's updates focus on visibility across the platform. Lakebase now logs every table change to Unity Catalog Delta tables, while SQL alerts notify teams when KPIs breach thresholds. The Excel add-in now serves HIPAA workspaces, and Google Sheets shows scheduled refresh history, bringing governed data to everyday tools.

digests.title: Lakebase autoscaling arrives on AWS
digests.intro: A new Lakebase version is now available on AWS, bringing autoscaling, scale-to-zero, database branching and instant restore. Teams can also use OpenAI's GPT-5, GPT-5 mini and GPT-5 nano models in Mosaic AI Model Serving, while Databricks SQL adds metric view metadata to DESCRIBE output.

digests.title: Metric views and AI agents take centre stage
digests.intro: Updates this period centre on giving AI agents governed access to data. Metric views now carry semantic metadata for Genie Agents and dashboards, and a managed SQL MCP server lets agents query Unity Catalog directly. Governance also tightened with certification tags and context-based ingress rules, while model choice widened with Claude Sonnet 4.5 and GPT-5.

digests.title: Spreadsheet access and Lakebase resilience take centre stage
digests.intro: This period brings Databricks data directly into Excel and Google Sheets, with metric views, SQL and scheduled refreshes now available to business users. Lakebase gains automatic failover across zones and support for compliance security profile workspaces, while customer-managed keys extend control over Unity Catalog data. GPT-5.4 also arrives via Model Serving for teams building AI applications.

digests.title: Multi-table transactions and agent-first pipeline development
digests.intro: Unity Catalog now coordinates managed Delta tables across engines, enabling multi-statement, multi-table transactions through catalog commits. Automatic identity management keeps users and groups in step with your identity provider, with Entra ID in Public Preview. Genie Code and Genie Agents extend agent-first work, from building and debugging pipelines to exporting metric views.

digests.title: Open Iceberg tables reach general availability
digests.intro: Managed and foreign Apache Iceberg tables are now generally available in Unity Catalog, giving teams open-format flexibility under one governance layer. Elsewhere, nested Supervisor Agents, fine-tuned LLM serving and billion-vector Vector Search endpoints extend what teams can build at scale.

digests.title: Genie One and agent tooling lead the way
digests.intro: Genie One dominates this period, now remembering user preferences and reporting conventions while serving finance teams as an AI coworker. Engineers gain a clearer route to production through the Agent Bricks CLI and horizontally scaled Databricks Apps. Governance also tightens, as external engines can now read governed Unity Catalog tables.

digests.title: Agentic analytics and governed AI take centre stage
digests.intro: This period's updates centre on making analytics more conversational and self-service. Genie Agent mode handles complex, multi-step questions, while imported Power BI and Tableau reports can now become AI/BI dashboards. On the platform side, Unity Catalog governance extends to hosted LLMs, Lakehouse//RT offers sub-second SQL, and Parquet v2 speeds up Delta tables.

digests.title: AI-driven governance and visual pipelines lead updates
digests.intro: This period's updates centre on making data easier to govern and build. Data Classification now uses an agentic AI system to find and tag sensitive Unity Catalog data automatically, while Lakeflow Designer lets teams build transformation pipelines visually using natural language. GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.5 Pro are also available pay-per-token through Mosaic AI Model Serving.

digests.title: Stronger governance and openness across the platform
digests.intro: Governing AI at scale leads this period's updates, with AI Gateway now enforcing access control and audit across MCP servers. Claude Opus 4.7 arrives on pay-per-token endpoints, while metric views now default to Builder mode and reach Google Sheets. Unity Catalog also opens to external Delta writers, alongside stronger encryption for Lakebase.

digests.title: Tighter access controls and unified AI observability
digests.intro: This period's updates centre on governance, with finer attribute-based masking, role-scoped access for sensitive data and a single trace table covering all AI activity. Teams also gain easier routes into Databricks, from importing Power BI and Tableau reports to writing Google Sheets back to Unity Catalog. Precision mode for ai_extract adds stronger handling of complex documents.

digests.title: Genie and Unity Gateway extend governed AI
digests.intro: Databricks is pushing governed AI further into everyday work, from coding agents connected through Unity Gateway to Genie apps, documents and spreadsheets. The Row Zero acquisition brings live spreadsheets into Genie, while Genie One lets any agent query data under Unity Catalog permissions. Together, these updates give data leaders central control over models, spend and access.

digests.title: OpenAI partnership brings models and agents to Databricks
digests.intro: Databricks and OpenAI have announced a $100 million partnership bringing OpenAI models natively to the platform, including Agent Bricks. LSEG's financial data is also now available within Databricks, helping teams build governed AI agents. Catalog Explorer's Assistant now turns natural language questions into SQL, while Databricks SQL 2025.30 adds session-scoped temporary metric views.

digests.title: Metric views and Claude models lead AI-driven updates
digests.intro: Metric views now sit at the heart of Databricks' AI and BI tooling, with Genie Agents and dashboards able to interpret them through semantic metadata. Claude Sonnet 4.5 is available pay-per-token, and prompt caching now covers Claude models. A new cybersecurity platform targets AI-driven threats.

digests.title: Databricks growth accelerates as AI tooling expands
digests.intro: Databricks reports over 65% year-on-year growth and a $5.4 billion revenue run-rate, backing Lakebase and Genie with over $7 billion of announced investment. Governance gets stronger with row filters and column masks in Lakeflow pipelines and schema-level anomaly detection in Data Quality Monitoring. Agent capabilities also advance, with Assistant connecting to MCP servers and Claude Opus 4.6 now hosted.

digests.title: Palantir alliance and Genie API widen AI reach
digests.intro: Databricks has announced a strategic partnership with Palantir, combining Palantir's AIP with the Data + AI Platform to speed up production AI and cut costs. The Genie Conversation API now lets developers ask questions, retrieve generated SQL and results, and query Genie Agents programmatically. Together, these point towards AI that is easier to build and run at scale.

digests.title: Databricks grows 55% and raises over $4 billion
digests.intro: Databricks passed a $4.8 billion revenue run-rate and is raising over $4 billion at a $134 billion valuation. Interoperability and governance are also key themes, with Delta Sharing now serving external Iceberg clients and admins gaining context-based ingress controls. Compute can now fall back to compatible instance types, and Lakeflow Connect adds a managed PostgreSQL connector.

digests.title: AI agents and governance take centre stage
digests.intro: Agent Bricks, MCP support and MLflow 3.0 show Databricks pushing AI agents into production, while Mosaic AI Gateway adds governance and monitoring. Partnerships with Google Cloud and Microsoft widen model choice, and Databricks One and Lakebase extend the platform to business users and operational apps. Unity Catalog's access controls and open table support keep governance consistent.

digests.title: MUFG Bank chooses Databricks for enterprise AI
digests.intro: MUFG Bank has selected Databricks as its next-generation data and AI platform, a move that brings its scattered AI model development under one roof. For data leaders, it is a clear signal that large financial institutions are consolidating fragmented AI efforts onto unified platforms. The decision highlights the growing priority of governed, scalable infrastructure for production AI.

digests.title: Databricks signs term sheet for Series K funding
digests.intro: Databricks has signed a term sheet for a Series K funding round that would value the company above $100 billion, with the round expected to close soon. For data leaders, the news signals strong investor confidence in the lakehouse platform and the company's capacity to keep investing in its roadmap.

digests.title: Databricks and Anthropic partner to bring Claude models
