digests.intro: Databricks and Anthropic have signed a multi-year partnership to bring Claude models directly to the Databricks platform. For data leaders, this means access to leading large language models alongside governed enterprise data, without moving information outside existing controls. It is a clear signal that model choice is becoming a core part of the data platform strategy.

digests.title: Databricks raises $15B to fund AI talent
digests.intro: Databricks has completed a $10B Series J equity round and closed $5.25B in additional debt financing, bringing its total funding to around $15B. The capital is aimed at attracting AI talent in a fiercely competitive market. For data leaders, it signals strong vendor stability and a continued race for AI expertise.

digests.title: Databricks brings marketing data and AI together
digests.intro: Databricks has launched data intelligence for marketing, a unified data and AI foundation that brings customer and campaign data together in one place. For data leaders, the release signals a push to move marketing analytics out of siloed tools and onto a shared governed platform. It offers a practical route to faster, more personalised campaigns built on a single source of truth.

digests.title: SAP Databricks arrives inside SAP Business Data Cloud
digests.intro: Databricks has released SAP Databricks, a product built natively into SAP Business Data Cloud. For data leaders, this brings Databricks' lakehouse capabilities closer to SAP business data, simplifying how enterprise teams analyse, govern and build AI on their SAP estate. It marks a notable step towards unifying SAP data with the wider platform.

digests.title: Databricks acquires BladeBridge to speed warehouse migrations
digests.intro: Databricks has acquired BladeBridge, bringing its technology and team on board to make moving existing warehouses onto Databricks SQL faster and less risky. For data leaders weighing the cost of legacy platforms, this points to a clearer, lower-effort route to consolidating analytics on the lakehouse.

digests.title: Databricks expands through acquisition and major funding
digests.intro: Databricks has acquired BladeBridge to accelerate migrations of legacy warehouses onto Databricks SQL, easing a common barrier for data teams. In parallel, it has raised substantial capital, combining a $10B Series J equity round with $5.25B in new debt to fund its AI ambitions and attract talent. For data leaders, this means simpler migrations and a well-funded roadmap.

digests.title: SAP Databricks arrives inside SAP Business Data Cloud
digests.intro: Databricks has released SAP Databricks, a product built directly into SAP Business Data Cloud. For data leaders, this offers a route to combine SAP business data with the lakehouse platform without heavy custom integration. It signals closer alignment between enterprise application estates and the data and AI tooling teams already rely on.

digests.title: Databricks to acquire serverless Postgres company Neon
digests.intro: Databricks has announced plans to acquire Neon, a serverless Postgres provider, strengthening its database offering. The move is aimed at developers and AI agents that need fast, elastic transactional storage alongside the lakehouse. For data leaders, it signals a push to bring operational databases and analytics closer together on one platform.

digests.title: Databricks to acquire Neon, expanding its database offering
digests.intro: Databricks has announced its intent to acquire Neon, a serverless Postgres company, to strengthen its database offering for developers and AI agents. Alongside this, the platform gains marketing-focused data intelligence and more consistent business metrics through Unity Catalog metric views. Genie also now offers richer table metadata controls, helping authors make their data easier to use.

digests.title: Databricks signs term sheet for Series K funding
digests.intro: Databricks has signed a term sheet for a Series K round valuing the company above $100 billion. Meanwhile, the platform continues to deepen its AI and governance capabilities, from Assistant running on Databricks-hosted models to governed tags and self-service access requests in Unity Catalog. Data leaders should also note the new SQL editor and expanded serverless GPU support.

digests.title: Databricks growth and agentic AI expansion
digests.intro: Databricks reported over 65% year-on-year growth and a $5.4 billion revenue run-rate, underlining momentum behind its AI and data platform. This period brought Claude Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 to Model Serving, a Supervisor Agent for multi-agent systems, and MCP support in Assistant. Governance also advanced with the Discover page, domains, and anomaly detection in Data Quality Monitoring.

digests.title: AI growth drives Databricks past $4 billion run-rate
digests.intro: Databricks reports a $4 billion revenue run-rate, with over $1 billion from AI. Agents now act as the querying user for tighter access control, while Assistant agent mode runs multi-step workflows from a single prompt. Low-latency feature serving and a Power Platform connector extend Databricks further into production and business applications.

digests.title: Databricks enters security with Lakewatch agentic SIEM
digests.intro: Databricks is entering the security market with Lakewatch, an agentic SIEM that brings unified data, petabyte-scale threat detection and investigations into one platform. Alongside this, the company is committing $850M to UK data and AI growth, quadrupling its office footprint and doubling its team. Genie One can now also search external sources such as Google Drive and SharePoint, with per-user authentication.

digests.title: Databricks pushes AI agents with governed data access
digests.intro: AI agents and their governance dominate this period, from Agent Bricks and the generally available Mosaic AI Gateway to MCP support through Unity Catalog. Lakebase adds a managed Postgres layer for AI apps, while Databricks One and Lakeflow Designer widen access for business users and analysts. Partnerships with Google Cloud and Microsoft extend model and cloud choice.

digests.title: Genie gains feedback tools as MUFG chooses Databricks
digests.intro: Databricks has strengthened Genie with a feedback revamp that lets users explain errors, regenerate answers or send responses for review, alongside support for customer-managed keys. Meanwhile, MUFG Bank has selected Databricks as its next-generation data and AI platform, consolidating scattered AI model development. Together, these updates point to greater governance, control and consolidation for data leaders.

digests.title: Databricks grows 55% and raises over $4 billion
digests.intro: Databricks passed a $4.8 billion revenue run-rate and is raising over $4 billion at a $134 billion valuation. Platform updates centre on Lakebase, which gains autoscaling, branching and scale-to-zero, alongside tighter access controls and wider interoperability through Delta Sharing for Iceberg clients. Data leaders also gain hosted GPT-5.2 and a generally available reranker for Vector Search.

digests.title: Databricks deepens AI partnerships with Anthropic and Palantir
digests.intro: Databricks has signed a multi-year partnership with Anthropic to bring Claude models to its platform, and a new Palantir alliance pairs AIP with the Data + AI Platform to speed production AI and cut costs. The Genie Conversation API also lets developers ask data questions programmatically and retrieve generated SQL and results.

digests.title: Genie agents expand with stronger governance
digests.intro: Genie agents now reach further, from a terminal coding tool to sandboxed code and external sources like Google Drive. Governance keeps pace through Unity Gateway guardrails, permission-aware apps and privilege-controlled skill sharing. Fox's multi-year commitment to Databricks underlines growing enterprise confidence.

digests.title: Genie agents gain models, web search and scheduling
digests.intro: Genie One and Genie Agents now use OpenAI models, search the public web and run scheduled prompts. Unity Gateway adds Anthropic Claude Fable 5.1 and OpenAI GPT-6 Astra, while attribute-based grants extend to models and MCP services. For data leaders, AI capability is widening, and governance is keeping pace.

digests.title: Governed data and memory for AI agents
digests.intro: Governed access to data is the common thread this period. Discover helps users find Unity Catalog assets, dashboards and Genie Agents by business area, while metric views gain query-time parameters. Managed long-term memory for AI agents extends Unity Catalog governance to agent state.

digests.title: Genie One brings natural-language data access to business users
digests.intro: Databricks has launched Genie One, a simplified interface that lets business users ask questions in plain language, view dashboards and use custom apps. For data leaders, the update signals a shift towards broader self-service access to governed data, reducing reliance on specialist teams for everyday insight.

digests.title: Metric views deepen as agent infrastructure matures
digests.intro: Metric views gain finer level of detail measures, window measures and conversion from SQL datasets. Unity Catalog ABAC policies now attach at metastore level, extending governance across every catalog. For agent builders, managed memory and Lakebase Search provide the storage and hybrid retrieval they need.

digests.title: Databricks plans strategic funding at $188 billion valuation
digests.intro: Databricks has signed a term sheet for strategic funding at a $188 billion valuation, led by Coatue. Governance featured prominently, with Unity Gateway now governing external model providers and MLflow traces moving into Unity Catalog. Practical gains include an agentic SQL converter for legacy dialects, Genie reaching Microsoft Teams, and a new Lakebase service level agreement.

digests.title: Microsoft partnership extended into the 2030s
digests.intro: Databricks and Microsoft have extended their partnership into the 2030s, deepening Azure use and native integration with Genie and Microsoft 365. Governance tightens with account-wide monitoring, context-based ingress control and role-based access for sensitive data. Genie Code now runs scheduled tasks, while Lakebase and Lakeflow add new troubleshooting and authoring tools.

digests.title: Genie Code brings agentic engineering to data work
digests.intro: Genie Code leads the updates, introducing autonomous production systems built from data engineering, data science and analytics ideas. Genie One now spans every workspace in an account and offers a unified chat that routes questions to the right agent. Runtime 18, Lakebase and Delta Lake transactions strengthen the platform, while dashboards now embed for external users.

digests.title: Lakebase Postgres gains autoscaling, branching and backups
digests.intro: Databricks has expanded Lakebase, its Postgres database, with autoscaling, scale-to-zero, instant branching, automated backups and point-in-time recovery, along with more regions. Genie One offers business users a simpler route to dashboards, natural language questions and custom Databricks Apps without technical skills. Dashboards also gain level of detail expressions, letting analysts control aggregation granularity for custom calculations.

digests.title: Genie arrives in Teams and Slack
digests.intro: Databricks is bringing its data intelligence closer to where people work, with Genie now answering data questions inside Microsoft Teams and Slack. Alongside this, the new OpenSharing protocol aims to make sharing data, models and agent skills open and interoperable. Governance and resilience also advance, with ABAC policies now covering models and managed disaster recovery extending to secondary regions.

digests.title: Governance and conversational analytics move centre stage
digests.intro: This period's standout theme is governance at scale, with Unity Catalog's attribute-based access control now applying row filters and column masks automatically from governed tags. Alongside it, Genie One brings chat to Public Preview and adds scheduled recurring prompts, lowering the barrier to self-serve data questions. Lakebase Provisioned also moves to Autoscaling, adding scale-to-zero and branching.

digests.title: OpenAI partnership and $4 billion revenue run-rate
digests.intro: Databricks and OpenAI have agreed a $100 million partnership bringing OpenAI models natively to the platform, as revenue run-rate passes $4 billion. Governed AI agents get tighter access controls and LSEG financial data, while Genie One eases access for business users.

digests.title: Lakebase, agent tooling and simpler business access
digests.intro: This period's updates focus on making Databricks more capable for AI agents and easier for business users. Lakebase Postgres gains autoscaling, instant branching and point-in-time recovery, while managed MCP servers let agents connect securely to Databricks resources. Genie One and Knowledge Assistant widen access to data, and serverless workspaces now arrive pre-configured.

digests.title: Agents gain tools, governance and spend controls
digests.intro: This period's updates centre on governed AI agents. Genie Agents now have generally available APIs and can call Unity Catalog functions, while Genie Code can run autonomously in Lakeflow Jobs. On the governance side, query text is masked by default, service principal secrets can be scoped, and agent skills become Unity Catalog securables.

digests.title: Unity Catalog opens to external engines and agents
digests.intro: Unity Catalog now reaches further, with external engines querying views and Spark writing to managed tables under governed control. Predictive AI Functions, Genie file upload and Document Intelligence put forecasts and document insights into everyday tools. Private Network Gateway also simplifies secure connectivity for data leaders.

digests.title: Unity Gateway puts AI models under governance
digests.intro: Unity Gateway now governs model services, MCP servers and model providers from one control plane, with spend budgets built in. Claude Code can route through it using existing Claude subscriptions, keeping governance intact. Packaged clean rooms also let partners analyse shared data privately.

digests.title: Unity Gateway and Genie One expand governed AI
digests.intro: This period's biggest theme is governance of AI at scale. Unity Gateway is now generally available, letting teams control, route and monitor AI services and MCP servers, while Genie One reaches Excel and Google Sheets and Genie Ontology is on by default. Admins also gained tighter control over serverless compute, secrets and tags, all within Unity Catalog.

digests.title: Cost controls and governance lead this update
digests.intro: Control is the headline: admins can now set budgets and per-user limits for Unity Gateway and Genie, and secrets are governed as Unity Catalog objects. Genie One gains citations and version history, while OpenAI's GPT-5.6 models now run pay-per-token on Model Serving.

digests.title: Account-level Genie One and stronger Unity Catalog governance
digests.intro: Genie One moves to account level in Public Preview, letting teams view dashboards, apps and Genie across workspaces from one place. On governance, customers can now encrypt Unity Catalog default storage with their own cloud KMS keys, and administrators can apply governed tags to catalogue objects. Genie Agents also gain friendly column names.

digests.title: Databricks raises $5 billion at $190 billion valuation
digests.intro: Databricks closed $5 billion in funding at a $190 billion valuation and passed a $7 billion revenue run-rate. This period's updates centre on governance, with finer access controls, sensitive data guardrails and more secure ways to share data. Teams also gain programmatic Lakebase management and Smart Routing to reduce AI costs.

digests.title: OpenSharing and Spark 4.3 headline new releases
digests.intro: Delta Sharing has been renamed OpenSharing and now covers tables, agent skills, AI models and unstructured data. Apache Spark 4.3 brings millisecond-latency streaming in Runtime 19, while Genie Migrate helps teams move classic jobs to serverless. Governance also tightens, with fine-grained read access in Lakehouse//RT and scope modifiers for tokens.

digests.title: Accenture and Databricks push enterprise AI agents
digests.intro: Accenture and Databricks are launching a business group with over 25,000 trained professionals to help clients deploy AI agents. Platform updates support that push, including Genie's automatic SQL checks, long-running tasks in Supervisor Agent, and GPU support on serverless compute. Real-time mode for Structured Streaming is now generally available on classic compute.

digests.title: Agents, governance and real-time data on Databricks
digests.intro: This period's updates centre on agentic AI, with Claude Opus 4.8 now served on Databricks and Genie One offering a managed MCP server for any agent. Governance tightens as Microsoft Entra ID identity sync removes SCIM provisioning and Unity Catalog access controls extend to external engines. Teams also gain real-time pipelines and simpler ingestion without change data capture.

digests.title: Genie gains new controls, pricing and customisation
digests.intro: Genie leads this period's updates, with new branding, personal skills and admin budget controls alongside a move to pay-as-you-go billing. Data leaders also gain governed external access to pipeline tables and materialised views through Unity Catalog, plus AI Search, which now supports full text indexing without embeddings.

digests.title: Microsoft partnership and agentic Genie expansion
digests.intro: Databricks has extended its Microsoft partnership into the 2030s and signed a term sheet at a $188 billion valuation. Genie now reaches Microsoft Teams, gains agent mode and runs scheduled tasks, while Unity Gateway and Governance Hub tighten control over models, spend and access. Migration tools for legacy SQL and Power BI lower the cost of switching.

digests.title: Databricks raises $5 billion as governance expands
digests.intro: Databricks closed $5 billion in strategic funding at a $190 billion valuation and passed a $7 billion revenue run-rate. The period's releases centre on governing AI, with Unity Gateway, sensitive data guardrails, and attribute-based policies extending to models and MCP services. Teams also gain tighter access controls, cross-workspace traffic rules and managed Iceberg and Delta Sharing options.

digests.title: Agentic AI spreads across the Databricks platform
digests.intro: Agentic AI leads this period's Databricks news, with Genie Code building production systems and Genie One spanning every workspace. Databricks also enters security with Lakewatch, an agentic SIEM, while Lakebase gains high availability for demanding workloads.

digests.title: Unity Catalog opens up Iceberg, agents and governance
digests.intro: Unity Catalog now generally supports managed and foreign Iceberg tables, multi-table transactions and attribute-based access controls for external engines, so governance follows your data across open formats and tools. Agent tooling also grew, with nested Supervisor Agents and a managed MCP server in Genie One. Identity sync from Microsoft Entra ID removes the need for SCIM provisioning.

digests.title: Genie expands agentic AI across tools and teams
digests.intro: Genie now spans search, agents and operations, reaching into Slack, Teams and ChatGPT with governed context. Unity Catalog gains Pages, metric views in Power BI and value lists, while Lakehouse//RT and Lakewatch extend the platform. A major EMEA investment across Europe and the Middle East underlines the push.

digests.title: Governed agents gain memory, GPUs and safeguards
digests.intro: AI Runtime is now generally available for GPU workloads, and agent memory improves quality while cutting cost and latency. Unity Gateway now governs desktop agents and screens MCP tool calls for jailbreaks and prompt injection. Per-user row filtering and CustomerLake's Beta round out a picture of agents working safely on governed data.

digests.title: Genie gains account-wide reach and governed sharing
digests.intro: Genie takes centre stage, with account-level Genie One now spanning Apps, Domains and Genie, plus shared agent skills for workspace teams. Data leaders gain simpler governance, as SAP semantic metadata syncs into Unity Catalog and foreign Iceberg tables can be shared via Delta Sharing. Builders benefit too, with apps deploying from Git and dashboards creating local metric views.

digests.title: Databricks goes agentic with CustomerLake and Genie One
digests.intro: Databricks is making agentic AI its central theme, launching CustomerLake and Genie One for business teams. It is also buying Panther to extend its security lakehouse, while Lakehouse//RT and LTAP target real-time analytics on one copy of data. For data leaders, governed data now serves both analytics and AI agents.

digests.title: Governed data reaches Excel, agents and partners
digests.intro: Governed data now reaches further into everyday tools and across organisations. Excel users can query Unity Catalog tables and write data back, while Genie gains MCP connectors for Google Drive, Gmail, Slack, GitHub and Microsoft 365. Sharing also extends to federated and Iceberg tables via OpenSharing.

digests.title: Databricks pushes agentic data and real-time analytics
digests.intro: Databricks has unveiled CustomerLake, an agentic customer data platform, and agreed to acquire Panther to extend its security lakehouse. Genie One now spans Teams, Slack, Copilot Cowork and mobile, while Lakehouse//RT brings millisecond queries to governed Delta and Iceberg tables. Governance also advances, with ABAC policies covering models and OpenSharing proposing an open standard for sharing data and AI.

digests.title: Unity Catalog governance and Genie One expand
digests.intro: Unity Catalog gains attribute-based access control, governed tags and customer-managed keys, while AI Gateway now governs MCP server interactions. Genie One reaches account level in Public Preview, bringing dashboards, apps and natural language questions across workspaces into one place. Together these updates let data leaders scale AI and self-service analytics with stronger control.

digests.title: Genie and agents deepen governed data work
digests.intro: Databricks is pushing Genie and agents deeper into daily data work, from spreadsheets and document pipelines to coding agents. Governance keeps pace, with Unity Catalog ABAC now applying across all catalogs and external secrets. For data leaders, agents can now act on governed data at scale.

digests.title: Governed AI agents across data and analytics
digests.intro: Databricks' latest updates centre on agents that work with governed data. Genie One, Genie Code and agent memory extend AI across analysis, coding and business tasks, while Unity Catalog extends access controls to external engines. Partnerships with SAP and Fox show enterprises standardising on the platform.

digests.title: Governed assets and easier migration across the platform
digests.intro: This period's updates centre on governance, with Unity Catalog now covering container images and offering impact analysis across lineage, and on getting existing estates onto Databricks, through Postgres migration to Lakebase and T-SQL conversion to Lakeflow pipelines. Teams also gain larger dashboard emails, connectors to Power BI and Tableau Cloud, and Gemini 4 Neon through Unity Gateway.

digests.title: Genie widens its reach across agents and migration
digests.intro: Genie now reaches beyond the workspace into Microsoft Copilot, Teams and Excel, while autonomous ZeroOps agents fix broken pipelines. Migration is easier too, with bulk moves from Tableau and Power BI and a serverless assessment tool that supports rollback. Governance keeps pace through Unity Catalog interoperability with Google Cloud and richer usage insight from Unity Gateway.

digests.title: Genie expands across tools, with major European investment
digests.intro: Genie now reaches the tools your teams already use, including Teams, Excel and Slack, through a unified Genie One workspace. Agents gain business context via Genie Ontology and MCP connectors, while ZeroOps detects and fixes broken pipelines. Databricks is also investing $3 billion across EMEA.
